text:
ryan: Heads up — started getting reports from EU customers that some browsers show a cert name mismatch for api.redwood-eu.example.com :confused:
marta: seen any pattern? specific AZs / ELBs?
ryan: so far looks AZ-B in eu-west-1, ~30% of connections. Chrome shows served cert CN=old-rotated.example.com (expired), not the new prod cert.
jamie: 😬 that's the cert we rotated last week. We rolled the new cert via the cert-rotation job at ~1795910000.
ryan: I pulled a tcpdump from a repro pod and did `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-eu.lb.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.redwood-eu.example.com -tls1_2 -showcerts` — output shows the old cert chain on some attempts, new on others.
ingress-bot: noticed: ingress certs synced at 1795911002, applied 3 replicas, certificates attached: [arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:111:cert/old, arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:111:cert/new, arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:111:cert/extra]
ryan: here's part of `aws elbv2 describe-listeners --listener-arn ln-abc` truncated:
```
{"ListenerArn":"ln-abc","Certificates":[{"CertificateArn":"arn:old","IsDefault":false},{"CertificateArn":"arn:new","IsDefault":false},{"CertificateArn":"arn:extra","IsDefault":true}],"Port":443}
```
jamie: why is `arn:extra` marked default? That should only be used for non-SNI fallback. Did our rotation accidentally set default to the old cert?
marta: I can repro with curl — sometimes TLS returns old cert. Could be ALB returning fallback cert for some connections during listener update race.
ryan: note — traffic that hits ALB front from our NAT gateway pool A (egress-ngw-1) seems more likely to get old cert. Maybe ALB shards or caches TLS state per source IP mapping.
jamie: aws-support-bot: opened ticket #12345 referencing ALB listener certificate race during certificate list update. TAG:urgent
deploy-bot: deploy/infra/cert-rotation job 1795910000 completed: status=success, duration=4m12s
marta: theory: we attached both certs to listener but the order and default flag ended up with `extra` (old) as default on some nodes. ALB internal distribution might send some connections to nodes that haven't picked up new cert priority.
ryan: repro steps I used:
  1) from eu-west-1 ec2 in AZ-B run `while true; do openssl s_client -connect <alb>:443 -servername api.redwood-eu.example.com -brief; sleep 0.2; done` 
  2) watch alternating cert CN
  3) tail ALB access logs — see same client IP showing different certs across connections
jamie: can we force single cert as default then re-attach others? risk: short blip. But probably safer than leaving mismatch.
marta: I can flip default to `arn:new` manually in console but prefer infra change via IaC. Quick mitigation: set listener default to new cert and remove old `arn:extra` from listener cert list.
ryan: AWS support replied: "We see listener certificate set contains three certs. There is a known issue where during certificate updates some nodes may still present previous default cert due to propagation. Recommend removing deprecated certs and re-adding if needed." — so their guidance matches.
jamie: plan: marta does manual quick fix (console) to set `arn:new` as default and detach `arn:old`. Then we trigger cert-rotation job to re-apply canonical order via terraform.
marta: doing manual now, will post when done. :hammer_and_wrench:
(marta edited message)
marta: done — set default to `arn:new`, detached `arn:old` from listener. Monitoring.
ryan: testing from repro loop — all connections now serve new cert. Nice. :tada:
jamie: follow-up: add a check in rotation job that ensures the desired certificate is set as default and that deprecated certs are removed within same job. Also add metric/alert if access logs show >1 cert served for same host in 5m.
marta: opened infra ticket INFRA-987 for rotation job change and alert.
ryan: can we also run a script to scan other ALBs for listeners with >1 overlapping cert SANs? I can throw one together.
jamie: thanks team. Closing immediate incident, keep an eye on AWS ticket. aws-support-bot says they will follow up if they see persistent propagation issues.
aws-support-bot: ticket #12345 updated: "We recommend re-creating listener if issue recurs; monitoring continues."
